questions.stem: The main objective of ethics in accounting is to

questions.stem: An accountant who does not disclose clients' information to unauthorised persons is observing the principle of

questions.stem: Integrity as an ethical principle requires an accountant to be
options: straightforward and honest in all professional relationships
questions.explanation: Integrity means honesty and fair dealing.

questions.stem: Objectivity requires that an accountant
options: does not allow bias, conflict of interest or undue influence to override judgement
questions.explanation: Professional judgement must be impartial.

questions.stem: Professional competence and due care require accountants to
options: maintain their knowledge and skills and act diligently
questions.explanation: Accountants must keep up to date and work carefully.

questions.stem: An accountant who accepts a gift to overlook errors in a client's accounts has violated the principle of

questions.stem: A professional accountancy body in Nigeria is

questions.stem: Professional behaviour as an ethical principle requires an accountant to
options: advertise services in a misleading way
comply with relevant laws and avoid actions that discredit the profession
disclose clients' affairs on social media
questions.explanation: Accountants must not bring the profession into disrepute.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a quality expected of a good accountant?

a club formed for social purposes

It is registered as a public company

credited to the joint venture account and debited to that venturer

questions.stem: Joint venture accounts differ from partnership accounts in that a joint venture

options: credited to the joint venture account
debited to the joint venture account as an expense

questions.stem: A partnership is formed by
options: two or more persons carrying on business in common with a view to profit
one person who owns all the capital
questions.explanation: This is the classic definition of a partnership.

questions.stem: The document that sets out the terms of a partnership is the

questions.stem: In the absence of a partnership agreement, profits and losses are shared

in the ratio of hours worked

questions.stem: In the absence of an agreement, partners are entitled to
options: salaries fixed by the senior partner
interest on capital at the bank rate
no interest on capital and no salaries
questions.explanation: Only equal profit sharing and 5% on loans apply.

questions.stem: The appropriation account of a partnership shows
options: the gross profit of the firm
the assets and liabilities of the firm
how net profit is shared among the partners
questions.explanation: It distributes profit.

questions.stem: Goodwill is
options: the cash balance of a firm
the value of a business's reputation and customer connections over and above its net assets
questions.explanation: Goodwill is an intangible asset.

Debit Goodwill ₦600,000; Credit X ₦300,000 and Y ₦300,000 capital accounts

questions.stem: On the admission of a new partner, assets are revalued so that
options: the new partner shares in past profits
gains or losses up to the date of admission belong to the old partners
questions.explanation: Revaluation profit/loss is shared in the old ratio.

options: transferred to a loan account if not paid immediately
questions.explanation: The firm owes the retiring partner.

questions.stem: The account opened to close the books on the dissolution of a partnership is the

in the ratio of their drawings
questions.explanation: This is the classic rule applied unless the agreement says otherwise.

questions.stem: When a partnership is converted into a limited company, the purchase consideration is
options: the total capital of the partners
the price paid by the company for the business of the partnership
the net profit for the year
the goodwill of the firm only
questions.explanation: It may be paid in shares, debentures or cash.

questions.stem: Drawings by partners are
options: debited to their current (or capital) accounts
shown as expenses in profit and loss
questions.explanation: Drawings reduce what the firm owes partners.

options: the firm owes the partner money
the partner has withdrawn more than his share of profits and other entitlements
the partner has made a loan to the firm
questions.explanation: The partner owes the firm.

questions.stem: A partner's loan to the firm is shown in the statement of financial position as
questions.explanation: It is separate from capital.

questions.stem: When a partner retires, his share of goodwill is
questions.explanation: He is entitled to his share of the goodwill he helped build.

questions.stem: If the partnership agreement provides interest on capital but the firm makes a net loss, the interest on capital is
options: still credited to the partners and the resulting larger loss shared in the profit-sharing ratio
charged to the profit and loss account as an expense
questions.explanation: Appropriations are made per the agreement, increasing the residual loss.

questions.stem: A company limited by shares is one in which
options: members' liability is limited to the unpaid amount on their shares
members guarantee a fixed sum on winding up only
questions.explanation: Liability is limited to the share capital subscribed.

questions.stem: A company limited by guarantee is commonly formed for
questions.explanation: Members guarantee to contribute an amount on winding up.

Share premium is classified as
questions.explanation: It cannot be distributed as cash dividend.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a revenue reserve?
questions.explanation: Revenue reserves come from retained profits and are distributable.

questions.stem: The key distinction between capital reserves and revenue reserves is that
options: capital reserves are created from trading profits
revenue reserves are shown as liabilities
capital reserves are always held in cash
revenue reserves can be distributed as dividends while capital reserves generally cannot
questions.explanation: Capital reserves arise from non-trading sources such as premiums and revaluations.

options: an expense charged before arriving at profit before tax
an appropriation of profit like dividends

questions.stem: Dividends paid to ordinary shareholders are
options: an expense in arriving at profit
questions.explanation: Dividends distribute profit to owners.

questions.stem: Transfer to general reserve is shown in the

questions.explanation: It retains profit in the business.

questions.stem: Debenture holders differ from shareholders because debenture holders
questions.explanation: They lend money to the company.

options: can offer its shares to the general public

questions.stem: Preliminary (formation) expenses of a company are
options: costs of forming the company, written off against profits
questions.explanation: They are written off as they have no realisable value.

questions.stem: A rights issue is
options: the free issue of shares from reserves
the sale of shares to directors only
an offer of new shares to existing shareholders in proportion to their holdings

questions.stem: The financial statements of a company are approved by shareholders at the

questions.stem: Public sector accounting deals with
options: the accounts of public limited companies
the recording and reporting of the financial transactions of government and its agencies
questions.explanation: It covers ministries, departments and agencies.

questions.stem: Under the cash basis of accounting, revenue is recognised when
questions.explanation: Cash basis ignores accruals.

questions.stem: The accrual basis of accounting recognises
options: only items approved by the legislature
revenues when earned and expenses when incurred
questions.explanation: Accruals match transactions to periods.

questions.stem: The fund into which all revenues of the Federal Government are paid, except those specified by law, is the
questions.explanation: It is created by the Constitution.

options: with the authority of an Appropriation Act or as provided by the Constitution
on the instruction of any minister
on the request of a bank
questions.explanation: Legislative approval is required.

questions.stem: The head of the treasury responsible for keeping the government's accounts and preparing its financial statements is the
questions.explanation: The Accountant-General manages the treasury.

questions.stem: The officer responsible for auditing the public accounts and reporting to the legislature is the
questions.explanation: The Auditor-General ensures accountability.

questions.stem: The chief financial officer of a local government is the
questions.explanation: The Treasurer manages local government finances.

questions.stem: The document issued by the Minister of Finance authorising the Accountant-General to release funds approved in the budget is the
questions.explanation: Warrants give authority to spend appropriated funds.

questions.stem: An Authority to Incur Expenditure (AIE) is issued
options: by the Auditor-General to the legislature
by an accounting officer to authorise a sub-officer to spend from a vote
by a bank to a customer
by the Central Bank to commercial banks
questions.explanation: AIEs delegate spending authority within approved votes.

questions.stem: Expenditure on the construction of a new hospital by government is
questions.explanation: It creates a durable asset.

questions.stem: Payment of salaries of civil servants is
questions.explanation: It recurs every period.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a source of government revenue?
questions.explanation: Taxes, fees, fines, licences, royalties and grants are government revenue.

questions.stem: Virement in public sector accounting means
options: transfer of savings from one sub-head to another within the same head with approval
questions.explanation: Virement reallocates approved funds.

questions.stem: The person responsible for the finances of a ministry, usually the permanent secretary, is called the
questions.explanation: Accounting officers answer for their ministry's spending.

questions.stem: Instruments of financial regulation in the public sector include
options: partnership deeds and articles of association
sales day book and cash book
the Constitution, Financial Regulations and the Appropriation Act
questions.explanation: These laws and rules govern public money.

questions.stem: The Contingencies Fund is used to
options: meet urgent and unforeseen expenditure for which no provision exists in the budget
questions.explanation: Advances are later regularised by supplementary appropriation.

questions.stem: A statement of assets and liabilities of government shows
options: the revenue collected during the year only
the financial position of government at a particular date
questions.explanation: It is the public sector equivalent of a balance sheet.

questions.stem: A major disadvantage of the cash basis of accounting in government is that it
options: does not show liabilities incurred but not yet paid
questions.explanation: Unpaid obligations are hidden.

questions.stem: Government budget is
options: a statement of estimated revenue and planned expenditure for a period
questions.explanation: Budgets plan public finance.

questions.stem: A computerised accounting system uses
options: computers and accounting software to record and process transactions
questions.explanation: Software automates processing.

questions.stem: The correct order of the data processing cycle is
questions.explanation: Data goes in, is processed, and information comes out (with storage).

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of computerised accounting over manual accounting?
options: Faster processing and fewer arithmetical errors
questions.explanation: Speed and accuracy are major advantages.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of computerised accounting is
options: the risk of data loss through viruses or system failure
questions.explanation: Systems need backups and security.

questions.stem: The keyboard and mouse are examples of
questions.explanation: They enter data into the computer.

questions.stem: A printer is an example of
questions.explanation: It produces hard copy output.

questions.stem: Accounting packages such as payroll and general ledger programs are classified as
questions.explanation: They perform specific user tasks.

questions.stem: The operating system of a computer is
options: system software that manages the hardware and runs other programs
questions.explanation: Operating systems control the computer.

questions.stem: Processing a group of similar transactions together at intervals, such as a weekly payroll run, is called
questions.explanation: Batch processing handles transactions in groups.

questions.stem: Making regular backup copies of accounting data is mainly to
options: increase the speed of the computer
enable recovery of data if the original is lost or corrupted
questions.explanation: Backups protect against loss.

questions.stem: Raw facts and figures that have not been processed are called
questions.explanation: Processed data becomes information.

questions.stem: A manual accounting system has the advantage that
options: it processes data faster than computers
it does not depend on electricity or computer equipment
questions.explanation: Manual systems are simple and cheap to set up.
